request: GET /api/ws  with Connection: Upgrade, Upgrade: websocket, Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13, Sec-WebSocket-Key: <16 bytes base64>
note: Seen three ways from this Mac over the tailnet: curl --http1.1 with the upgrade headers gives 403 and no body; curl over HTTP/2, which cannot upgrade, gives the REST 401 with its JSON body instead; URLSessionWebSocketTask gives NSURLErrorBadServerResponse with task.response.statusCode 403. So a client that probes the socket with a plain GET learns the wrong thing: only a real upgrade over HTTP/1.1 reaches the denial. The proxy adds its security headers to both answers, and the 403 carries no reason a client could read.
